metadata.design_note: Questions never determine eligibility; they populate the attribute set consumed by the deterministic SER rule engine (database primacy).

questions.question_text: Welcome! What would you most like to achieve right now?
questions.help_text: Pick the goal that matters most today. You can explore other goals later.

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Great choice. Let's find the best support available for this.

questions.question_text: Are any of these also on your mind? Pick as many as apply.
questions.help_text: This helps us surface bonus opportunities you were not looking for.

questions.question_text: When do you want to act on this goal?
questions.help_text: Some schemes have application windows, so timing matters.

questions.question_text: Roughly how much financial support are you looking for?
questions.help_text: A rough range is perfectly fine — this shapes which schemes fit.

questions.question_text: What kind of support appeals to you most?
questions.help_text: We will still show everything you qualify for — this sets the ranking.

questions.question_text: Have you ever applied for a government scheme before?
questions.help_text: No judgement either way — it simply tells us how much guidance to give.

questions.question_text: How did that earlier application go?
questions.help_text: If something went wrong before, we will help you avoid it this time.

questions.question_text: Which type of scheme did you apply to earlier?
What has been the biggest obstacle to your goal so far?
questions.help_text: We rank schemes higher when they remove your specific obstacle.

questions.question_text: How confident do you feel about navigating government schemes today?
questions.help_text: We adapt how much explanation we give based on this.

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Noted. We will pitch every explanation at the right level for you.

questions.question_text: Which of these best describes you?
questions.help_text: This single answer shapes the entire conversation ahead.

options.label: Employee or advisor representing a business

questions.question_text: Are you exploring this for yourself, or on behalf of someone else?

options.label: For a client (I am a CA / consultant)

questions.question_text: What is your role in the organisation?
Are you an Indian citizen?
questions.help_text: Most Indian government schemes require Indian citizenship.

questions.question_text: Where do you currently live?
What is your age?
questions.help_text: Several schemes have age windows — for example, many startup and self-employment schemes favour applicants between 18 and 45.

questions.question_text: How do you identify?
questions.help_text: Some excellent schemes are reserved for women and transgender entrepreneurs. Sharing this can only unlock options, never remove them.

questions.question_text: What is your marital status?
questions.help_text: A few welfare and self-employment schemes have specific provisions here.

questions.question_text: Do you have a disability (Divyangjan)?
questions.help_text: Persons with disabilities get reserved quotas and higher subsidies in many schemes.

questions.question_text: What is the disability percentage on your certificate?
questions.help_text: Benefits typically begin at 40% certified disability.

options.label: I do not have a certificate yet

questions.question_text: Which social category do you belong to?
questions.help_text: SC/ST/OBC applicants unlock reserved quotas and enhanced subsidies. This never reduces your options.

questions.question_text: Do you belong to a notified minority community?
questions.help_text: Notified minorities: Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Parsi, Jain.

questions.question_text: Does your household hold a BPL (Below Poverty Line) card?
What type of ration card does your household have?
What is your family's total annual income?
questions.help_text: Income ceilings decide eligibility for many subsidy and welfare schemes. A band is enough — no exact figure needed.

questions.question_text: And your own annual income, roughly?
Do you currently file income tax returns?
questions.help_text: Some schemes require ITRs; a few welfare schemes exclude taxpayers.

questions.question_text: What is your highest education level?
questions.help_text: A few loan-linked schemes have minimum education requirements (often 8th pass).

questions.question_text: Do you hold any technical or professional qualification?
Are you an ex-serviceman or a dependent of one?
questions.help_text: Defence veterans get reserved quotas in several self-employment schemes.

questions.question_text: Would you be the first entrepreneur in your family?
questions.help_text: Some schemes, like PM-YUVA and Stand-Up India, celebrate first-generation entrepreneurs.

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: First-generation founders get special attention in several schemes — good news for you.

questions.question_text: Are you a member of a Self Help Group (SHG)?
questions.help_text: SHG members can access group-linked credit and enterprise schemes.

questions.question_text: Are you registered under any urban livelihood mission (e.g. NULM)?
Does your household hold an MGNREGA job card?
Do you have a valid caste certificate?
questions.help_text: Category benefits require a certificate at application time — we will add it to your checklist if needed.

options.label: Yes, but it may need renewal

questions.question_text: Do you have an EWS income & asset certificate?
Do you live in a notified tribal (Scheduled) area?
questions.help_text: Scheduled areas attract special sub-plans and higher assistance rates.

questions.question_text: What best describes your current occupation?
questions.help_text: Government employees are excluded from a few self-employment schemes, so this saves you wasted effort.

questions.question_text: Which state or union territory are you based in?
questions.help_text: State schemes often stack on top of central schemes — location can double your options.

options.label: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.question_text: And which district?
questions.help_text: A few districts enjoy special status that unlocks extra benefits.

questions.question_text: Is your location rural, semi-urban, or urban?
questions.help_text: Rural units often get higher subsidy percentages — for example 35% vs 25% under PMEGP.

questions.question_text: Is your district on the Government's Aspirational Districts list?
questions.help_text: Aspirational districts get priority processing and enhanced support. If unsure, choose 'not sure' — we will verify it for you.

questions.question_text: What is your PIN code?
questions.help_text: Used only to match location-specific schemes — never shared.

questions.question_text: Will your business or project operate in the same district you live in?
Which state will the project or business operate in?
questions.help_text: Eligibility follows the project location, not your home address.

options.label: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.question_text: Is (or will) your unit be located in a notified industrial area or park?
questions.help_text: Units in notified industrial estates often get power, land, and infrastructure benefits.

questions.question_text: Is your unit inside an SEZ or registered as an EOU?
Would you consider locating in a different area if incentives were significantly better?
questions.help_text: Some states compete hard for new units — this tells us whether to show you those offers.

questions.question_text: Where does your business journey stand today?
questions.help_text: Every stage has schemes designed for it — there is no wrong answer.

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Perfect — there are schemes built precisely for this stage.

questions.question_text: What is the legal form of your business?
questions.help_text: Some schemes require a company or LLP; others welcome proprietorships too.

questions.question_text: Which year was the business registered or started?
questions.help_text: Business age decides startup-scheme eligibility (usually under 10 years) and vintage requirements for loans.

questions.question_text: Is your business registered on the Udyam portal (MSME registration)?
questions.help_text: Udyam registration is free, takes 10 minutes, and is the master key to most MSME schemes.

questions.question_text: Is the business GST-registered?
questions.help_text: Many subsidies are disbursed against GST-linked turnover records.

questions.question_text: Does the business have its own PAN?
In one line, what does (or will) the business do?
questions.help_text: Your own words — we will map them to official categories for you.

ux.placeholder: e.g. We manufacture cotton garments for export

questions.question_text: How many operating units or locations do you have?
Do you hold a factory license or Shops & Establishment registration?
How many years of experience do you have in this line of work?
questions.help_text: Experience strengthens loan applications and some schemes require it.

questions.question_text: Is this a family business or connected to one?
Do you have a written business plan or project report?
questions.help_text: Most loan-linked schemes need a project report — we can flag templates and help.

options.label: It is all in my head for now

questions.question_text: What is your current monthly revenue, roughly?
Is the business currently profitable?
Does the business have a current account in its own name?
How many years of business ITRs have been filed?
questions.help_text: Banks typically want 2–3 years of ITRs for larger loans; new units have new-unit schemes instead.

questions.question_text: How many years of audited financial statements do you have?
Which of these registrations do you already hold?
questions.help_text: Existing registrations shorten your document checklist — nice head start if you have them.

questions.question_text: What percentage of the business do you (the applicant) own?
questions.help_text: Several schemes require the applicant to hold a majority stake.

questions.question_text: Is this a brand-new unit, an expansion, or a takeover of an existing unit?
questions.help_text: Subsidy schemes treat new units, expansions, and revivals very differently.

options.label: Takeover / purchase of an existing unit

questions.question_text: What is your total investment in plant, machinery, or equipment (excluding land and building)?
questions.help_text: Use the original purchase value. An estimate within 10–15% is fine — this sets your MSME class (Micro / Small / Medium).

questions.question_text: What was your annual turnover in the last financial year?
questions.help_text: Turnover is the second half of MSME classification and drives loan and subsidy ceilings.

questions.question_text: And the year before that, roughly?
questions.help_text: Growth trend matters for some credit schemes. An estimate is fine.

questions.question_text: How would you describe your turnover trend over the past 3 years?

options.label: Business is too new to say

questions.question_text: Does your turnover figure include export sales?
questions.help_text: Export turnover is excluded from MSME classification — which can keep you in a lower, more benefit-rich category.

questions.question_text: What classification does your Udyam certificate show?
How much additional investment are you planning in the next 12 months?
If a registration (like Udyam or GST) unlocks a scheme, are you willing to complete it?
questions.help_text: Almost always free or low-cost — and we will tell you exactly which one is worth doing.

questions.question_text: What is your (or the business's) approximate net worth?
Do you currently have any business loans outstanding?
What is the total outstanding loan amount?
How is the repayment on existing loans going?
questions.help_text: Honest answers here protect you — default history affects credit-scheme eligibility, and we will point you to revival schemes if needed.

questions.question_text: Do you know your credit (CIBIL) score range?
questions.help_text: No credit history is not a barrier — several schemes are built for first-time borrowers.

questions.question_text: Could you offer any collateral if a loan required it?
questions.help_text: If you have no collateral, collateral-free guarantee schemes like CGTMSE become your best friends.

questions.question_text: How much of the project cost can you contribute from your own funds?
questions.help_text: Most subsidy-linked loan schemes expect 5–10% promoter contribution; special categories often get relaxations.

questions.question_text: Have you received a government capital subsidy for this unit before?
questions.help_text: Some schemes bar double-dipping on the same asset — others happily stack. We will sort that out.

questions.question_text: Could you arrange a third-party guarantor if required?
Which type of bank do you primarily deal with?
How long have you banked with them?
Has a bank declined a loan application of yours in the past 2 years?
questions.help_text: If yes, we will prioritise schemes with guaranteed cover that make banks say yes.

questions.question_text: Do you carry informal debt (moneylenders, chit funds) you would like to replace?
questions.help_text: Several schemes explicitly help swap expensive informal debt for cheap formal credit.

questions.question_text: Does the business have any insurance coverage?
What share of your revenue comes through digital payments?
questions.help_text: Digital transaction history is becoming an alternative to collateral in newer credit schemes.

questions.question_text: What exact funding amount will you apply for, if you know it?
questions.help_text: Optional precision — it lets us match scheme ceilings exactly. A blank is fine; we will use your earlier range.

questions.question_text: Which sector is your business (or idea) in?
questions.help_text: The single biggest branching point — manufacturing, services, and trading each have distinct scheme families.

questions.question_text: Which manufacturing area fits you best?
questions.help_text: Sector-specific schemes (like PLI) can dwarf generic ones — this is worth answering carefully.

questions.question_text: Which services area fits you best?
Would your activity count as a khadi, village, or coir industry?
questions.help_text: Village industries (units in rural areas, often traditional crafts) unlock KVIC-family schemes with generous margins.

questions.question_text: Are you a traditional artisan or craftsperson (e.g. weaver, potter, carpenter, blacksmith)?
questions.help_text: Schemes like PM Vishwakarma are built exclusively for traditional trades.

questions.question_text: Does your business involve any of these: tobacco, pan masala, alcohol, or gambling?
questions.help_text: Being upfront saves time — most schemes exclude these activities, and we would rather not waste your effort.

questions.question_text: Do you know your unit's pollution category?
questions.help_text: Red-category units face extra clearances; white-category units skip most of them.

questions.question_text: Do you know your NIC activity code (from Udyam/GST)?
questions.help_text: Optional — if you have it handy it sharpens matching; if not, your plain-language description is enough.

questions.question_text: Who do you mainly sell to?
questions.help_text: Selling to government? Public procurement preferences for MSMEs may apply to you.

questions.question_text: Is the business seasonal?
Where do your key raw materials come from?
questions.help_text: Import-dependent units qualify for different support than local-sourcing ones.

questions.question_text: Roughly what percentage of your production capacity are you using today?
questions.help_text: Above 80%? Expansion schemes fit. Below 50%? Working-capital and market-linkage support may matter more.

questions.question_text: Is this a franchise of another brand?
Do you sell through e-commerce platforms (Amazon, Flipkart, ONDC, your own site)?
questions.help_text: Onboarding support and digital-commerce schemes exist for MSME online sellers.

questions.question_text: Are you registered on GeM (Government e-Marketplace) or supplying to government?
questions.help_text: MSMEs get exemptions and purchase preference in government procurement.

questions.question_text: How many people work in your business today, including you?
questions.help_text: Count everyone — full-time, part-time, and family members who work in the business.

questions.question_text: How many of them are women?
questions.help_text: Higher women employment boosts eligibility and subsidy rates in several schemes.

questions.question_text: How many employees are from SC/ST communities, if you know?
Do you employ any persons with disabilities?
questions.help_text: Incentives exist for employers of persons with disabilities, including EPF reimbursement.

questions.question_text: How many new people do you plan to hire in the next 12 months?
questions.help_text: Employment-linked incentive schemes reward net new job creation.

questions.question_text: Is your establishment registered with EPFO?
questions.help_text: EPFO registration is the gateway for employment-linked incentive claims.

questions.question_text: And with ESIC?
What is your workforce mostly made of?
Do you currently engage apprentices under NAPS/NATS?
questions.help_text: The government reimburses a share of apprentice stipends — a low-risk way to grow your team.

questions.question_text: Roughly what share of your workers are from your local district?
questions.help_text: Some state incentives require a minimum share of local employment.

questions.question_text: What is the average monthly wage you pay?
questions.help_text: Some employment incentives apply only to employees below a wage ceiling.

questions.question_text: Will most new hires be first-time formal-sector employees?
questions.help_text: First-time EPFO enrollees attract the richest employment incentives.

questions.question_text: Where do you stand on exports?
questions.help_text: There are schemes for every stage — from first-shipment handholding to freight support for veterans.

questions.question_text: Do you have an Import Export Code (IEC)?
questions.help_text: The IEC is a 10-minute online registration and the first key to every export benefit.

questions.question_text: What share of your turnover comes from exports?
For how many years have you been exporting?
Which markets are you targeting?
Do you hold an RCMC (membership of an Export Promotion Council)?
questions.help_text: RCMC membership is required for several export incentives — and councils themselves offer market support.

questions.question_text: Do you use ECGC export credit insurance?
What will you export?
What is your biggest export hurdle right now?
questions.help_text: Each hurdle maps to a different support scheme — buyer-seller meets, certification subsidies, credit, or freight support.

questions.question_text: Would you attend international trade fairs if most of the cost were reimbursed?
questions.help_text: Market development schemes reimburse a large share of stall and travel costs for MSMEs.

questions.question_text: Do you currently use pre- or post-shipment export credit?
Are you enrolled in any Districts-as-Export-Hubs or state export programme?
Are you planning to buy machinery or equipment?
What is the estimated machinery cost?
questions.help_text: Capital subsidy schemes have slabs — the amount decides which slab and which scheme.

questions.question_text: Will the machinery be new or second-hand?
questions.help_text: Most subsidy schemes fund only new machinery — important to know before you commit.

questions.question_text: Will it be Indian-made or imported?
questions.help_text: Some schemes give an extra margin for indigenous machinery.

questions.question_text: Is this an upgrade of existing technology or fresh capacity?
Do you need land for this project?

options.label: No — I have my own land/premises

questions.question_text: Does the project include constructing or renovating a building?
What is the total project cost, all-in (land, building, machinery, working capital)?
questions.help_text: This is the number banks and schemes anchor on — your best estimate is enough.

questions.question_text: When do you plan to start implementation?
By how much will this expand your capacity?
questions.help_text: Several expansion schemes require at least 25% capacity addition to qualify.

options.label: It is an entirely new product line

questions.question_text: Do you need any shared or industrial infrastructure?
Is your unit part of an industry cluster (many similar units nearby)?
questions.help_text: Cluster development schemes fund shared facilities that individual units could never afford alone.

questions.question_text: Will you need a loan for this?
How much loan do you need?
questions.help_text: Loan size instantly narrows the field: up to ₹10 lakh, ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore, and above each have different flagship schemes.

questions.question_text: What will the loan mainly fund?
What repayment period would suit you?
How important is a collateral-free loan to you?
Is your margin money (own contribution) ready in hand?
questions.help_text: Margin readiness is one of the top predictors of quick loan sanction.

questions.question_text: Did you know some schemes refund part of your loan interest?
questions.help_text: Interest subvention schemes can cut your effective rate by 2–3% or more.

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Now you do — and we will check every one of them for you.

questions.question_text: Have you taken a MUDRA loan before?
questions.help_text: A well-repaid MUDRA loan is a springboard to the next, larger category.

questions.question_text: Have you already approached a bank for this loan?
questions.help_text: Some subsidies must be claimed before sanction — timing matters a lot here.

questions.question_text: How confident are you about servicing the EMI from business cash flows?
questions.help_text: An honest answer helps us right-size the loan schemes we recommend.

questions.question_text: Which digital tools does your business use today?
What would you digitise first if cost were not a barrier?
Have you heard of or enrolled in ZED (Zero Defect Zero Effect) certification?
questions.help_text: ZED Bronze is currently free for MSMEs and unlocks subsidy top-ups in other schemes.

questions.question_text: Would you join a subsidised lean-manufacturing improvement programme?
questions.help_text: Lean consultants at 90% government cost — typically 10–20% productivity gains.

questions.question_text: Does the business own any intellectual property?
Are you planning to file for a patent, trademark, or design?
questions.help_text: MSMEs and startups get steep fee discounts and reimbursement for IP filings.

questions.question_text: Does your business do any research or product development?
Roughly what share of turnover goes into R&D?
Do you collaborate with any university, IIT, or research lab?
questions.help_text: Industry-academia projects unlock co-funded technology development grants.

questions.question_text: Do you need help finding or licensing a technology?
Would you describe any of your products or processes as genuinely new to the market?
Would structured mentoring or incubation support help you right now?
Which quality certifications do you already hold?
Which certification are you planning to obtain?
questions.help_text: Certification cost reimbursement schemes cover a large share — often 50–75% of your expense.

questions.question_text: Is your product under mandatory BIS certification (like toys, electronics, helmets)?
questions.help_text: If yes, certification is not optional — but subsidy support makes it far cheaper.

questions.question_text: Do you use NABL-accredited labs for product testing?
Is your product from a GI-tagged region or craft (like Banarasi silk, Darjeeling tea)?
Do you use barcoding / GS1 registration on your products?
questions.help_text: Barcode registration fees are reimbursable for MSMEs — a small but real saving.

questions.question_text: What holds you back from certification?
Do your target export markets demand specific certifications?
Is your startup DPIIT-recognised?
questions.help_text: DPIIT recognition is free and unlocks tax exemption, self-certification, and the Startup India ecosystem.

questions.question_text: What makes your venture innovative?
questions.help_text: DPIIT recognition requires working towards innovation or improvement — most genuine ventures qualify.

questions.question_text: Can the business scale without costs growing at the same pace (e.g. software, platforms)?
Are you associated with any incubator or accelerator?
questions.help_text: Seed Fund Scheme money flows through approved incubators — association matters.

questions.question_text: What is your funding history so far?
How much external funding have you raised in total?
What stage is your product at?
questions.help_text: Prototype-stage ventures fit seed grants; scaling ventures fit growth capital and market access.

questions.question_text: Which space is the startup in?
Has the startup won any grants, awards, or competitions?

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Excellent — prior recognition strengthens almost every application.

questions.question_text: Are any founders currently students or recent graduates (within 5 years)?
questions.help_text: Student founders unlock campus-linked pre-incubation and innovation grants.

questions.question_text: Are the founders working on this full-time?

options.label: It is a side project for now

questions.question_text: Are you comfortable giving equity in exchange for government-linked seed investment?
questions.help_text: Seed Fund support comes as both grants (for prototypes) and convertible instruments (for market entry).

questions.question_text: Do you have a pitch deck and financial projections ready?
Would you join a structured government accelerator cohort if selected?
What percentage of the business is owned by women?
questions.help_text: 51%+ women ownership is the magic threshold for most women-entrepreneurship schemes.

questions.question_text: Is day-to-day management led by a woman?
questions.help_text: Some schemes require women to hold operational control, not just shareholding.

questions.question_text: Is the enterprise linked to a women's Self Help Group or federation?
Are you a member of any women-entrepreneur association (FICCI-FLO, WICCI, local chamber)?
Have you explored women-specific schemes before (like Stand-Up India or Mahila Udyam)?

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: Either way — we will lay out every women-focused option you qualify for.

questions.question_text: Would workplace facilities support (creche, hostel, transport) be valuable to your unit?
Do you or your family actively farm?

options.label: Yes — we cultivate our own land

questions.question_text: How much agricultural land does the family hold?
questions.help_text: Land holding decides your farmer category (marginal / small / other) — and with it, subsidy percentages.

questions.question_text: Do you hold a Kisan Credit Card (KCC)?
Do you receive PM-KISAN instalments?
questions.help_text: PM-KISAN enrolment doubles as identity proof of farmer status in several other schemes.

questions.question_text: Are you a member of an FPO (Farmer Producer Organisation) or co-operative?
questions.help_text: FPOs unlock collective schemes with far larger grants than individual ones.

options.label: Yes — and I am an office bearer

questions.question_text: What do you mainly grow or deal in?
What processing activity are you doing or planning?
Do you need cold storage or cold-chain infrastructure?
Do you already run a micro food processing unit (even informal/home-based)?
questions.help_text: Existing informal units are the priority target of formalisation schemes like PMFME — being small and informal is an advantage here.

questions.question_text: Is your product your district's ODOP (One District One Product) item?
questions.help_text: ODOP alignment gives priority and better terms under food-processing schemes.

questions.question_text: Are you into (or entering) dairy, poultry, goatery, or fisheries as a business?
Do you need farm machinery (tractor, harvester, drone) for yourself or as a rental business?

options.label: As a rental / custom hiring business

questions.question_text: What is your irrigation situation?
What post-harvest infrastructure would help you most?
What is your monthly electricity/energy bill, roughly?
What powers your operations today?
Are you considering solar or other renewables?
What rooftop solar capacity are you considering?
questions.help_text: Subsidy structures differ sharply by capacity slab — a rough range is enough.

questions.question_text: Have you ever done a professional energy audit?
questions.help_text: Subsidised energy audits typically find 10–20% savings — and audit reports unlock efficiency-upgrade loans.

questions.question_text: Would you upgrade to energy-efficient equipment if part of the cost were subsidised?
Are electric vehicles relevant to your operations (delivery, staff transport, fleet)?
How do you handle production waste?
questions.help_text: Waste-to-value and circular-economy schemes turn disposal costs into revenue.

options.label: It is a real problem for us

questions.question_text: Do you use water recycling, rainwater harvesting, or ETP?
Interested in green certifications (GreenCo, green building, carbon accounting)?
Where is your team's biggest skill gap?
What training format works for your team?
Do YOU want training for yourself (entrepreneurship, management, a trade)?
questions.help_text: Free EDP training is mandatory in some loan schemes — and genuinely improves survival rates.

questions.question_text: How many people would you want trained?
Would government-certified skill certificates (NSQF) matter to you?
Or are you looking to BECOME a training provider/partner yourself?
questions.help_text: Training-partner accreditation is its own opportunity category with per-candidate funding.

questions.question_text: What is your current research position?
What type of institution are you affiliated with?
Which field is your research in?
Do you currently hold a fellowship?
What research output do you have so far?
Do you want to commercialise your research?
questions.help_text: Translational grants (like BIRAC BIG or NIDHI-PRAYAS) sit exactly at this research-to-market bridge.

questions.question_text: How mature is the technology?
What do you need funding for?
What form does (or will) your social organisation take?
Does the organisation have 12A / 80G registration?
questions.help_text: 12A/80G status is the gateway to most institutional and CSR funding.

questions.question_text: Is it registered on NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog portal)?
questions.help_text: NGO Darpan ID is mandatory for almost all government grants to NGOs.

questions.question_text: Are you seeking CSR funding from companies?
Who does your work primarily serve?
How long has the organisation been operational?
questions.help_text: Most government grants require a 3-year track record; younger organisations fit CSR and incubation routes.

questions.question_text: Quick document check — do you have your Aadhaar handy and linked to your mobile?

ux.acknowledgement_on_answer: That is the single most important document sorted.

questions.question_text: Personal PAN card?
An active bank account with Aadhaar seeded?
questions.help_text: Direct benefit transfers land only in Aadhaar-seeded accounts — easy to fix at your branch if not.

questions.question_text: Address proof for the business location (rent agreement, utility bill, or ownership papers)?
A recent income certificate from the revenue authority?
questions.help_text: Needed only for income-linked schemes — issued by your Tehsil office, usually within days.

questions.question_text: Land records (7/12 extract, khatauni, or lease deed) for any land involved?
Passport photos and a scanned signature?
Vendor quotations for machinery or assets you plan to buy?
questions.help_text: Two to three quotations are standard for any capital-linked application.

questions.question_text: Are your documents scanned as PDFs/images under 1 MB each?
questions.help_text: Ninety percent of portal errors are oversized files — we will give you exact size specs per scheme.

questions.question_text: Are key documents (bank account, premises) in your own name?
questions.help_text: Name mismatches are the #1 silent rejection reason — better to know now.

questions.question_text: Almost done! If you had to pick, what matters most in our recommendations?
questions.help_text: We will show everything you qualify for — this just sets what appears on top.

questions.question_text: How much hand-holding would you like at the application stage?

options.label: I will apply myself with your checklist
I would pay for full application support

questions.question_text: Which language should your recommendation report be in?
When do you realistically plan to submit your first application?
May we alert you when a new scheme matches your profile or a deadline approaches?
questions.help_text: Scheme windows open and close through the year — alerts mean you never miss one.

questions.question_text: Finally — is everything you shared accurate to the best of your knowledge?
